title: Valence - Embeddings & Reranking Discovery
header: Date: 2026-07-07T15:00Z; Duration: 42m; Location: Zoom; Recording: enabled; Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Valence CTO), Priya Rao (Valence ML Eng), Marcus Lee (Valence Infra), Aisha Khan (Valence PM)
summary: Intro discovery to understand Valence's embedding-based reranking needs. Primary goals: integrate vector DB, candidate generation throughput, dimensionality choices, hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings), and deployment preference (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). Security and compliance questions surfaced (SOC2, KMS, data residency). Agreed to run a 2-week PoC on a subset of user queries and share security docs + preliminary pricing.
topics: hosting options: hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC
transcript: 00:00 Sam (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
00:06 Liam (Valence): Liam here, CTO. Good to be here.
00:08 Priya (Valence): Priya, ML eng. Hi all.
00:11 Marcus (Valence): Marcus, infra. Morning.
00:14 Sam: Awesome. Maya from infra/serving side will join to cover throughput/benchmarks. Maya, over to you for a 30k foot on how Redwood handles embeddings/rerank flows?

00:22 Maya (Redwood): Yeah, sure. So typically we split the flow into two phases: candidate generation via ANN in a vector DB or our hosted ANN, then a reranker — usually a cross-encoder — for final score and ordering. We support hybrid search patterns: BM25 for recall + embeddings for semantic matching. On hosting, we can run this on Redwood Hosted for convenience, Dedicated reserved GPU pools for consistent latency, or Private inside a customer's VPC for regulated data.
00:45 Priya: Quick q — when you say vector DB, you mean you integrate with Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate, or you have your own store?

00:53 Maya: Both. We have integrations with Pinecone, Milvus, and similar. We also offer an embedded nearest-neighbor service in hosted mode that's optimized for our runtime. For Private/Dedicated customers we typically recommend plugging into their in-cluster Milvus or self-hosted Faiss for max control.

01:10 Liam: Our current stack is Elasticsearch for BM25 and Faiss prototype for vectors. The problem is at scale: candidate gen is fine but reranking with a cross-encoder kills latency, and cost is climbing. We're looking at batching, candidate size, dim tradeoffs — any rules of thumb?

01:26 Maya: Yeah so typical pattern: candidate set of 50-200 hits from ANN, then reranker on top. Cross-encoders are expensive — we recommend quantized models or running the reranker on Dedicated GPUs to keep p99 latency reasonable. Also, embedding dimensionality matters: 1536 dims (OpenAI ada2-like) gives richer representation but increases ANN size and index memory; 512 dims can be a sweet spot for throughput while preserving quality in many cases.
01:53 Priya: We're using 1.2M docs, average doc length is 300 tokens. We target 200 qps peak for candidate gen and 50 qps for rerank at 95th percentile. Does Redwood Dedicated handle that?

02:06 Maya: Yes, Dedicated is designed for predictable throughput. We can size GPU pools and set autoscaling policies. For 200 qps candidate gen and 50 rerank qps, you'd be looking at a couple of worker instances with batching and KV cache enabled. We also do prefix caching so repeat prefixes don't re-run large sections.
02:22 Marcus: Are there limitations on vector dimensionality in your hosted ANN? We don't want to downsample embeddings if possible.

02:29 Maya: Hosted supports up to 2048 dims; higher dims increase memory and nearest-neighbor latency. For super high dims we recommend using an external vector DB tuned for high-dim indices (e.g., HNSW in Milvus) and connecting via our integration.
02:45 Aisha: Regarding hybrid search, we want to preserve keyword precision for legal queries plus semantic recall. How do you recommend combining BM25 and embeddings?

02:54 Sam: Common approach is BM25 to produce a high-recall candidate set (say top 200) then rerank that set with embeddings similarity and cross-encoder adjustments. Another is linear fusion where you normalize BM25 and cosine scores. We can prototype both and measure MRR on your eval set.
03:12 Priya: On the reranker model, you mentioned cross-encoder vs bi-encoder. We're leaning cross-encoder for quality but need latency help. Any batching/quantization tips?

03:21 Maya: For cross-encoders, batching across candidates reduces per-query overhead — Redwood supports dynamic batching. Quantization (int8/4-bit) also reduces GPU memory and increases throughput; we have recommendations per architecture. Another option is a two-stage reranker: cheap bi-encoder re-score then a sparse cross-encoder for top 10.
03:40 Liam: Security is non-negotiable. Do you have SOC2 and KMS integrations? Our legal will ask about audit logs and customer-managed keys.

03:47 Sam: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs. Dedicated includes audit logging and RBAC; Hosted supports encryption-at-rest and managed KMS. We'll share the security pack after the call.
04:00 Marcus: If we go Private in our VPC, can we keep everything on-prem? We have some air-gapped workflows.

04:06 Maya: We have an on-prem package and a VPC Private option. Air-gapped is possible but introduces additional ops. For many customers, Private in their cloud VPC with a private control plane is the balance — you keep keys and network restrictions.
04:18 Priya: Benchmarks — do you have examples for 512 vs 1536 dims throughput with HNSW? We're trying to trade accuracy for cost.

04:26 Maya: We do. Rough numbers: with HNSW and optimized kernels, 512-dim indexes are typically 2-3x denser in QPS for a given memory footprint vs 1536 dims. But quality delta depends on task. We recommend running an eval: embed a representative sample with both dims and compute recall@k and MRR.
04:42 Liam: Integrations — we want to keep Elasticsearch in the loop for metadata and BM25, Faiss for internal experiments, and maybe Pinecone for hosted. Any pitfalls?

04:51 Maya: The main pitfalls are keeping consistent embedding models and dimensionality across systems and sync between index updates. We'll help with ingestion patterns: batch upserts, realtime streams, and nearline rebuilds. Also watch index memory and choose appropriate index params (efConstruction/efSearch for HNSW).
05:06 Priya: For PoC, what's a realistic dataset size? We can supply 50k docs and a query set of 2k labeled pairs. How fast can you run an A/B?

05:14 Sam: That's perfect. We can run a 2-week PoC: week 1 ingestion & baseline runs, week 2 reranker tuning and metrics. We'll set up a sandbox on Dedicated or Hosted depending on your preference; Private would take longer to provision.
05:27 Marcus: Cost — we need top-level numbers to budget. Can you send a pricing range for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
05:33 Diego (Redwood CSM): Yep, we'll send a preliminary pricing sheet. It'll include token costs, GPU-hour estimates for Dedicated, and approximate infra fees for Private.
05:41 Aisha: Any known competitors we should watch? We're evaluating Pinecone, Milvus and a managed OpenSearch setup.
05:47 Sam: Competitors commonly mentioned: Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, and some customers use OpenSearch/Elastic with k-NN. We'll include a short comparison in the follow-up docs.
06:00 Priya: One more technical — for reranking, how do you handle cold-start for new docs? We have lots of frequent updates.

06:08 Maya: We support incremental upserts and nearline reindexes. For heavy update loads, we recommend a hybrid where realtime docs go into an in-memory overlay and we periodically rebuild the ANN index.
06:19 Liam: Ok let's recap next steps so legal and infra can move fast.

06:22 Sam: Recap: Redwood to share security pack (SOC2, encryption, KMS options), send preliminary pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, run a 2-week PoC with 50k docs and 2k queries, schedule a technical deep dive on reranker latency and batching. Valence to confirm dataset and internal stakeholders for PoC. Any deadlines?
06:44 Liam: We'd like proposals by next Tue 2026-07-14 if possible.
06:48 Sam: Sounds good. We'll aim for that. Thanks everyone.
06:52 Priya: Thanks.
06:54 Meeting end
